definitions.full: H6455. pisseach מִּסֵּחַ adjective lame ; — absolute ׳פ 2Sam 9:13 +; plural מִּסְחִים 5:6 +; — as attributive Lev 21:18 (+ עִוֵּר ); predicate 2Sam 19:27 , ׳פ רַגְלָיו שְׁתֵּי 9:13 lame as to both his feet ; compare also (of animal) Deut 15:21 (+ עִוֵּר ); as substantive 2Sam 5:6 , 8 (twice in verse); Jer 31:8 ; Mal 1:8 , 13 ; Job 29:15 (all + עִוֵּר ), also Isa 33:23 ; 35:6 ; Prov 26:7 .

occurrences.englishText: For whatever man he is that has a defect, he shall not draw near: a blind man, or a lame, or he who has a flat nose, or any deformity,
If it has any defect—is lame or blind, or has any defect whatever, you shall not sacrifice it to Yahweh your God.

David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him go up to the watercourse and strike those lame and blind, who are hated by David’s soul.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame can’t come into the house.”

So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem; for he ate continually at the king’s table. He was lame in both his feet.
He has slandered your servant to my lord the king, but my lord the king is as an angel of God. Therefore do what is good in your eyes.
I was eyes to the blind,
Like the legs of the lame that hang loose,
Then the lame man will leap like a deer,
Behold, I will bring them from the north country,

When you offer the blind for sacrifice, isn’t that evil? And when you offer the lame and sick, isn’t that evil? Present it now to your governor! Will he be pleased with you? Or will he accept your person?” says Yahweh of Armies.

You say also, ‘Behold,‡ “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection. what a weariness it is!’ and you have sniffed at it”, says Yahweh of Armies; “and you have brought that which was taken by violence, the lame, and the sick; thus you bring the offering. Should I accept this at your hand?” says Yahweh.
